scope: Actual GitHub Markdown rendering in Chromium, with whole-document DOM inspection and selected visual checks; not a mathematical proof.

findings: Ten bracket-delimited display formulas were not recognized.
Ten double-dollar display formulas adjoined ordinary paragraphs and were not recognized.
Fifty Japanese inline expressions and one English expression remained literal dollar-delimited text.
Ordinary Markdown consumed TeX backslashes, including the thin-space command in the Hamiltonian sign diagnostic.

rounds.finding: The GitHub renderer rejected operatorname in seven expressions. Counting renderer elements alone would have missed the failures.
rounds.repair: Use the explicitly reviewed mathop/mathrm/nolimits expansion for the plain operator names im, Log and diag.

visual_checks: English target 0.6: both display equations, inline image operator, hypotheses and prose flow.
Japanese target 0.9: the complete Gronwall bound and both accompanying definitions fit the inspected content area.
Japanese target 8.4: canonical Barnes product, asymptotic polynomial and explicit remainder bound.
Japanese appendix: scalarization formula and the two-by-two matrix with its diagonal operators.
specific_payload_checks: The Hamiltonian diagnostic contains a MathML mspace of width 0.167em and no literal comma in place of the thin space, in both languages.
The Japanese tube-set formula retains both set braces and both double norm bars.
The image operator is an upright MathML operator, and the matrix has two rows and four cells.

local_tex_parser_comparison.limitation: The one unconverted expression in each language contains d_{\rm phase}, unsupported by this local TeX parser. Actual GitHub renders both successfully, so the existing source was retained.
local_tex_parser_comparison.distinction: Pandoc GFM math-node recognition passed for every formula; this limitation belongs to its separate TeX-to-MathML converter.

limits: Visual inspection used the recorded desktop viewport; this is not a claim about every browser or screen width.
Ordinary Unicode mathematical prose is outside the marked-TeX inventory.
This review validates presentation, not the truth or proof completion of the mathematical targets.
